name: Leuprorelin
route_note: IM or SC depot injection every 1, 3, 4 or 6 months; daily SC solution historically
owner: AbbVie (Lupron Depot, US); Takeda (outside US); Tolmar (Eligard); generic daily injection

discovery.note: A nonapeptide GnRH analogue with D-leucine at position 6 and an ethylamide at the C terminus, giving greater potency and resistance to degradation than native GnRH.

tagline: GnRH agonist depot used for prostate cancer, endometriosis and early puberty
summary: Leuprorelin (leuprolide) is a synthetic GnRH analogue that, after a brief surge, desensitises pituitary GnRH receptors and suppresses LH, FSH and sex hormones to castrate levels. It is a standard androgen-deprivation therapy for prostate cancer and is also used for endometriosis, uterine fibroids, central precocious puberty and breast cancer ovarian suppression.
mechanism: Leuprorelin binds pituitary GnRH receptors more strongly and for longer than native GnRH. Initial stimulation produces a 'flare' of LH, FSH and testosterone or oestradiol for 1–2 weeks.

Continuous exposure then causes receptor downregulation and desensitisation, so gonadotrophin secretion falls and testosterone reaches castrate levels within about 2–4 weeks. Antiandrogens are sometimes given at the start to prevent flare symptoms in metastatic prostate cancer.
uses: Premenopausal breast cancer (ovarian function suppression, outside US label in some regions)

history.title: GnRH structure
history.detail: Andrew Schally's group determines the structure of GnRH; Schally and Roger Guillemin share the 1977 Nobel Prize.

history.title: Leuprorelin synthesised
history.detail: Takeda scientists report highly potent GnRH analogues, including leuprorelin.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Daily injectable Lupron approved for advanced prostate cancer.

history.title: Depot formulation
history.detail: Monthly Lupron Depot microsphere formulation approved (TAP Pharmaceuticals, a Takeda–Abbott venture).

history.title: Precocious puberty
history.detail: Lupron Depot-Ped approved for central precocious puberty.

history.title: TAP settlement
history.detail: TAP Pharmaceuticals pays $875 million to settle US federal charges over Lupron marketing and Medicare pricing.

history.title: Camcevi
history.detail: A ready-to-use 6-month SC leuprolide mesylate formulation is approved.

pk.half_life: about 3 hours (IV/SC solution); depot gives sustained release over 1–6 months
pk.bioavailability: IM/SC well absorbed; not active orally

common: loss of libido and erectile dysfunction

facts: The INN is leuprorelin; 'leuprolide' is the US adopted name used on American labels.
